cases.query: I can collect whole experimental trajectories and ask a different generator for continuations. My target may not have exact low rank, but its future rows at each cut are nearly contained in a small probability-valued span. Can I acquire one finite sampler without supplying those rows or a noise estimate?

My teacher only draws futures at prefixes it can actually reach. I cannot request its tiny probabilities, and adding a probability floor might send a query to an impossible prefix. Is there a consistent finite cached law that respects this access restriction?

Every next symbol remains bounded away from zero and each noisy readout retains a positive information fraction. Does this protect a hidden bit encoded over a long sequence, or can an efficiently computed global distinction still disappear?

An unknown noisy quantum encoder has a recoverable intrinsic part but faithful ambient outputs. Can I acquire a program before the payload arrives and later decode an already encoded state without calling the original source again? What quantum memory and consistency does that require?

I receive independent premade Choi states but cannot coherently preprocess the logical inputs of the source calls. Can I use the random-dilation factory to acquire a late-payload recovery program anyway?

I have local quantum instrument calibration and a noncommuting extensive control potential. Can a finite patch certify the trajectory bound with a complete numerical commutator tail, and which theorem and code originals are actually available?

I want to choose a quantum recovery resolution before risking an unknown payload. A held-out Bell test worked in one shared frame. What exactly can I carry forward, and how does abort probability enter the conditional error?

For a live quantum instrument under adaptive feedback I already have positive operator inequalities for exponential recorded rewards. Can they give a bound valid at arbitrary stopping times without assuming mixing or reconstructing the conditional state?
